answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and scoped to the primary region while settlement writes are at peak, so the closest prior win is regional failover (b2), which restored latency in minutes without failing the write path. Circuit breaking (b4) would shed customer writes and is rejected. Rollback (b1) remains a live alternative because a release shipped two hours ago, but region confinement is the stronger discriminator than release timing, and a gradual 90-minute climb is not yet proven to be the build. Failover of settlement writes still carries replication/consistency risk, so that downstream-value hazard is flagged and b2 should be re-read before the shift. Uncertainty remains across release regression vs regional saturation vs infra; this choice prioritizes keeping writes succeeding on a healthy region.
